items.rule: The game is for 2 to 5 players (age 8+).
Remove the 4 quick-rules cards from the deck and set them aside as a guide for the game.
Shuffle the remaining cards and deal 5 cards face down to each player.
Players look at their cards and keep them hidden from the others.
The rest of the cards are placed face down in the middle as the draw pile.
The youngest player starts and play proceeds clockwise.
Step 1 of a turn: draw 2 cards from the draw pile and add them to your hand.
If you have no cards in hand at the end of your turn, draw 5 cards at the start of your next turn (instead of 2).
Step 2: you may play up to 3 cards from your hand onto the table; playing 1 to 3 cards, or none, is allowed (not obligatory).
Type A: place money cards (and/or action cards) in a bank pile in front of you; this money is used to pay debts.
An action card placed in the bank becomes money permanently and can never be used as an action card for the rest of the game.
Type B: place property cards face up in front of you to build color groups; each card shows how many properties make a complete group (2, 3 or 4).
You may start as many color groups as you want.
Type C: play action cards by following their instructions and placing them in the center next to the draw pile; an action card drawn during your turn may be played immediately or kept for later.
Step 3: at the end of your turn you may hold at most 7 cards in hand (table cards don't count); excess cards go under the draw pile.
When paying a debt, cards are never transferred into a player's hand; they go to the receiver's bank or property area.
You can never pay with cards from your hand; only cards laid on the table in front of you (bank and properties) can pay.
The payer chooses how to pay: bank cards, property cards, or a combination.
No change is given: if you overpay, you lose the excess.
Property cards used for payment are placed by the receiver among their own properties on the table.
If you have no cards on the table to pay a debt, you pay nothing.
Deal Duel (Forced Deal style): take a property card from any player, except one that is part of a complete group.
Deal Troc: swap one of your properties with one of another player's properties (not from a complete group).
Deal Banco: take a complete property group (including buildings) from any player.
Joker! cancels an action played against you and can be used at any time; the other player can cancel your Joker with their own Joker.
Deal Jackpot: claim 5M from a player of your choice; It's My Birthday: every player gives you 2M.

Rent cards: two-color rent makes every player pay rent for one of your property groups matching one of the card's colors; the multicolor rent card charges 1 player of your choice for any of your properties.
Double Rent is played together with a rent card to double the amount claimed.
House/Hotel: add to a complete group to increase rent (house +3M, hotel +4M); only one house and one hotel per group, hotel only after a house, and not on railroads or utilities.
Pass Go card: draw 2 cards; several can be played in the same turn (within the 3-card limit).
Property Wild cards substitute for a missing property of their colors; the 2 multicolor wilds can replace any color but have no monetary value and cannot be banked.
At the start of your turn, if you draw a property of the same color as a wild you have placed, you may swap them to take the wild back into your hand or place it on another group.
The game ends when a player has 3 complete property groups of different colors.
You can only win on your own turn; if you realize you've completed 3 groups during another player's turn, you must wait until your next turn to declare victory.
There is no point scoring; money is only used to pay debts, and the goal is to be first to own 3 complete property groups of different colors.
The winner is the first player to have 3 complete property groups of different colors.
For 6 or more players, shuffle 2 Monopoly Deal decks together; the rules stay the same.
